I recorded the restriction in the motor-pool inspection log this morning, but the fleet status board hasn't been updated yet. This means the 3,800-kilogram engineering pallet cannot go on V-2 — it'll have to go on V-1, and the 1,800-kilogram general stores can go on V-2.

transcript.text: SFC Alvarez's constraint makes sense to me. With V-2 limited to 3,000 kilograms, the 3,800-kilogram engineering pallet has to go on V-1, and the 1,800-kilogram general stores fit fine on V-2. So the full assignment would be: V-3 carries the 1,200-kilogram refrigerated medical crate, V-1 carries the 3,800-kilogram engineering pallet, and V-2 carries the 1,800-kilogram general stores. All weights are within each vehicle's effective payload rating. From a logistics standpoint, that plan is sound — but I'd note that the manifest worksheet still needs to be updated to reflect V-3 for the medical crate, and SFC Alvarez should make sure the fleet status board gets updated for V-2's suspension restriction before we depart.
